title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a case of a perception system used outside the conditions it was built for. An automated licence plate reader produced an alert that did not correspond to the vehicle in front of the officers: the image matched a Chevrolet Malibu while the plate was read on a red Dodge Ram pickup. The failure happened at the point of deployment, where a camera output was treated as a positive identification rather than as a lead requiring confirmation, and the stop escalated from there.

Catching this would have required a human check against the vehicle itself before the stop was treated as a stolen-plate stop. The mismatch between the recorded vehicle type and the observed vehicle was available to officers at the roadside. The department's own K-9 policy, which requires handlers to weigh the severity of the crime, immediate threat, and whether a suspect is resisting or evading, is a separate judgement made after the stop had already begun.

What is not established is how the misread occurred, whether the camera or its matching logic was at fault, and whether any finding of wrongdoing will follow. The department's investigation found no wrongdoing in the K-9 deployment, and charges against the driver were later dropped according to his lawyer. A report of an alert is not proof that a plate was stolen, and an investigation's conclusion is not a verdict on the underlying technology.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police Department officers are under investigation after body camera footage was released showing a K-9 being released on a driver during a traffic stop. The stop began after a FLOCK camera alert about a stolen license plate, but the alert was wrong. The camera image matched a Chevy Malibu while appearing on a red Dodge Ram pickup truck. The driver, Brandon Upchurch, was stopped, ordered out at gunpoint, and arrested on charges of resisting arrest and obstruction. He received medical attention at the scene.

Officers later realized the plate information was a misread and was not stolen. Police said they believed the driver might flee and did not know if he or the passenger had weapons. Department policy requires handlers to weigh the crime's severity, any immediate threat, and whether a suspect is resisting or trying to evade arrest before deploying a K-9.
